course_description:
In ARCS3010, you'll be guided through each stage of archaeological field-based research, from research design through excavation and laboratory analysis to professional report writing. You'll do this through the excavation of a simulated archaeological site right here on the grounds of the UQ St Lucia campus. At every stage, you'll be asked to think and work as a practising archaeologist would, making the same decisions and facing the same constraints as you would in real fieldwork.

ARCS3010 is taught in intensive mode across Weeks 1–10 of semester, during which time you'll build skills in:

These skills are developed through a blend of self-paced online learning and hands-on fieldwork at UQ’s purpose-built Archaeology Teaching and Research Centre (ATARC). The course has three main learning components:

Weeks 1–3, Build your foundations : Work through online learning modules and the course readings, which cover the theory and method behind key areas of archaeological field practice.

Weeks 4–7, ATARC excavation : This is where you get to apply your online learning to an authentic fieldwork training experience. In small groups, you'll excavate a simulated archaeological site at the ATARC (Building 56J), applying excavation, recovery, and recording methods in the field. Working as a team member is an essential part of a professional archaeologist’s job, and this course also gives you the opportunity to dig and learn together as a group.

Weeks 8–10, Making sense of your results : Back in the Archaeology Teaching Laboratory (Michie 325), you'll continue to work with your group to analyse the finds and data from your excavation and share your group's results with the class. You’ll also have self-paced online GIS activities and report writing modules to work through to help you analyse your fieldwork spatial data and prepare your excavation report.

Participation Requirements

The fieldwork at the heart of this course makes it an authentic training ground for archaeological practice. Your presence and participation in the practicals are therefore an inherent requirement and are essential for meeting the course's learning objectives. As such, attendance is compulsory. If illness or another circumstance keeps you from attending one of the ATARC practicals, please provide a medical certificate or other acceptable supporting documentation to student.socsci@uq.edu.au — without this, your mark may be affected as outlined in the Assessment section. If you find yourself missing two or more of the ATARC practicals, we strongly encourage you to consider withdrawing from the course (check the University Academic Calendar for withdrawal dates to avoid academic or financial penalty).

Course Details

ARCS3010 is a 2-unit, 3rd-level course, required for the Bachelor of Arts Extended Major in Archaeology and the Bachelor of Science Major in Archaeological Science. Because this course is designed to prepare you for 4th year Honours and for careers in professional archaeology, it asks more of you than a 2000-level course — both in the standard of scholarship expected and in your readiness to engage. You must be at 3rd year equivalent in archaeology and have completed the course pre-requisites to enrol.

Course Communication

All course communication will be via Blackboard Announcements and your student email, so please check both regularly. If you'd like to meet me outside class times to discuss your progress in the course, please send me an email ( a.crowther@uq.edu.au ) to arrange an appointment.

Australian Archaeology Skills Passport

ARCS3010 is designed to align with the Australian Archaeology Skills Passport , a national record of practical archaeological competencies used across the discipline for professional practice. assessment_details.task_description: Completion of group excavation notes including all recording forms, registers, photographs, and safety forms from the ATARC excavation. The field notes are completed in class during the ATARC practicals, and are submitted to the Course Coordinator at the end of each practical class. They are not taken home or able to be worked on outside of class time. The final notes are submitted for marking at the end of the final ATARC class in Week 7. The notes are completed in small groups (excavation teams) of 4-8 students depending on class size. Students must work together in their groups to ensure all field notes are completed and accurate. Field notes are marked on a group basis and each student's individual mark is then calculated by multiplying the group mark by their Peer Assessment Factor (PAF) following the guidelines set out in the Peer Evaluation assessment item. This assessment item is cumulatively worth 20 marks (5 marks x 4). If a student is absent from the practical classes without an acceptable reason and therefore cannot contribute to the field notes, the student cannot gain marks for that weeks’ field notes contribution (5 marks). Marking criteria: Criteria including rubrics are available in the ‘Assessments’ folder on the course Blackboard site. AI Use: This assessment task will be completed in-person. assessment_details.title: Peer Evaluation
assessment_details.other_conditions: Peer assessment factor. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: A Peer Assessment Factor (PAF) is a score that assesses the contribution made by each group member to the group’s field notes according to the extent of their participation in the excavation and recording of the excavation notes. Each student must evaluate all group members’ contribution using the online Peer Evaluation form on Blackboard. The scores are confidential and not shared with the group members. Forms must be completed by each student and will be available on Blackboard after the end of class in Week 7 and must be submitted by the due date. PAFs will be calculated using the following formula: A student’s PAF = ∑ scores from peer evaluation forms divided by 100 The PAF is then used to adjust each student's individual mark for the Field Notes assessment as follows: For PAFs > 1.1 : Individual mark for assignment = 1.1 x Group mark (i.e. maximum of 10% mark-up) to a maximum of 20 marks total for the Field Notes; For PAFs ≤ 1.1: Individual mark for assignment = PAF x Group mark (i.e. a mark directly proportional to the contribution as assessed by self and peers collectively). Students who receive a PAF score of less than 0.7 may be given an opportunity to provide appropriate explanations about their low level of contribution from the groups’ perspective. The Course Co-ordinator can moderate the PAF to ensure fairness. Marking criteria: Criteria including rubrics are available in the ‘Assessments’ folder on the course Blackboard site. assessment_details.title: Excavation Report
assessment_details.task_description: Excavation report covering all aspects of the ATARC excavation. This assessment is completed individually (NOT in excavation groups) and requires the compilation of data drawn from a background literature review and the primary data recorded during the excavation to form a final excavation report. Rather than being purely descriptive, this report must also include critical evaluation and interpretation of this material. The word limit for this assignment is 3500 ± 10% words. Additional details on how to prepare the report will be provided via Blackboard/Inspera. Marking criteria: Criteria including rubrics are available in the ‘Assessments’ folder on the course Blackboard site. AI Use: This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI technologies, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which AI may provide limited support and guidance. A failure to reference AI use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct Policy. Students may be required to complete an AI usage declaration and submit it with their assessment. Additional resources are available through UQ AI Student Hub . learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 3 (27 Jul - 16 Aug)
learning_activities.topic: Weeks 1–3: Online Modules #1-6 Complete online learning modules. Topics covered are: (1) What is Field Archaeology (and introduction to Research Design). (2) Finding Sites. (3) Stratigraphy. (4) Excavation and Recovery. (5) ATARC methods. (6) Spatial data. (Note: Modules 1–6 should be completed before the first practical class at the ATARC. Additional modules covering GIS analysis will be made available later in the course). Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L05

Week 1: Course Introduction (Zoom check-in) Join me on Zoom in Week 1 for a Course Introduction. This is a chance to ask any questions about the course before we formally meet in Week 4. Learning outcomes: L01

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 4 To Week 7 (17 Aug - 13 Sep)
learning_activities.topic: Weeks 4–7: ATARC Excavation Site excavation at the ATARC. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 8 To Week 9 (14 Sep - 27 Sep)
learning_activities.topic: Weeks 8–10: Finds Analysis and Group Presentation Work in your groups to analyse your ATARC finds. At the end of Week 9, each group will give a short informal presentation to the class about their excavation results and interpretations. Class Location: Michie 325 Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 8 To Week 10 (14 Sep - 11 Oct)
learning_activities.topic: Weeks 8–10: Online Module #7 (GIS) Module 7 comprises a series of QGIS activities including: (i) Creating a locality map of the ATARC and other sites in the Moreton Region. (ii) Creating a contour map of the ATARC site. (iii) Plotting artefact proveniences and creating heat maps using total station data collected during the ATARC excavation. (iv) Georeferencing and rectifying excavation photos. (v) Preparing and presenting GIS data in your final Excavation Report. Instructions on how to download and install QGIS are included in the module. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05

Week 9: In-Class Exam Examination of content from the online modules and required readings, and the application of general concepts and knowledge across all course content. The exam will take place in-class during the scheduled laboratory practical. Exam Location: Michie 325 Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L05
